readings: Count each rating's films in stock as the number of inventory copies (inventory rows joined to film, grouped by rating). Find the ratings whose copy count is above the mean copy count across all ratings. Return one row with the total copies across those ratings and the average amount by which their copy counts exceed that across-rating mean, with no rounding.

Count each rating's films in stock as the number of distinct films with at least one inventory copy (COUNT DISTINCT film_id, grouped by rating). Find the ratings whose distinct-film count is above the mean distinct-film count across all ratings. Return one row with the total distinct in-stock films across those ratings and the average amount by which their distinct-film counts exceed that across-rating mean, with no rounding.
queries:
WITH rc AS (
  SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS copies
  FROM inventory i
  JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
m AS (
  SELECT AVG(copies) AS mean_copies FROM rc
)
SELECT SUM(rc.copies) AS total_copies,
       AVG(rc.copies - m.mean_copies) AS avg_excess
FROM rc, m
WHERE rc.copies > m.mean_copies;
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT i.film_id) AS cnt
  FROM film f
  JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
m AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) AS mean_cnt FROM counts
)
SELECT SUM(c.cnt) AS total_distinct_films,
       AVG(c.cnt - m.mean_cnt) AS avg_excess
FROM counts c, m
WHERE c.cnt > m.mean_cnt;
